Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. Branch: feature/SFCC-91_pdp-colour-swatches. This is a fix round on SFCC-91 Step 3, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/`. Do not stage, do not commit. Do not touch any other file. Do NOT use `git stash` under any circumstances (a prior agent used it against explicit instruction this session; it turned out harmless but must not be repeated — use file reads and `git diff`/`git status` only for any before/after comparison you need).

## The bug, confirmed via real Chromium rendering by a prior Tester round

The component's outer container (`root`) has no width of its own — by design, so it can size naturally to however many swatches are showing when NOT paginated. But this means the label row (which shows "Colour: {name}") has no width ceiling to truncate against either. A long colour name just makes the whole component grow wider than the swatch row beneath it, with nothing clipping it — the truncation CSS (`overflow:hidden; textOverflow:ellipsis; whiteSpace:nowrap` on the `labelName` part) is correctly written but structurally has nothing to truncate against unless some ANCESTOR happens to impose a definite width. Confirmed empirically: wrapping the same rendered component in an external 350px-wide container caused clipping to actually occur; without that wrapper, a 70-character name rendered at full width with the label/chevrons visibly detached from the 192px swatch row beneath.

**Marcel's decision, already made — implement exactly this:** cap the component's own width to the same reserved 4-swatch footprint that pagination already uses (`calc(4 * var(--zimm-scale-1200))`, 192px), unconditionally — not just when paginated. This makes truncation self-contained and correct in every context, regardless of what the eventual PDP page (Step 4, not yet built) does or doesn't constrain.

## The fix

Read `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts` in full first. It already has a constant (from the immediately prior rework round) for the paginated width — likely named something like `PAGINATED_SWATCHES_WIDTH` and set to `calc(4 * var(--zimm-scale-1200))`, currently applied conditionally to the `swatches` part's `width`/`minWidth` only when `isPaginated` is true. Find its exact current name.

Apply this SAME value as a `maxWidth` on the **`root`** part, **unconditionally** (not gated behind `isPaginated` — it should apply in every case, paginated or not). Use `maxWidth`, not `width` — a `maxWidth` lets the component remain naturally narrower when content is short (e.g. one or two colours with short names), while guaranteeing it can never grow WIDER than the reserved swatch-row footprint, which is exactly the ceiling the truncation CSS needs. Do not change `width` on `root` or on anything else — only add `maxWidth`.

If a single shared constant makes sense now that it's used in two places (the paginated `swatches` width and this new `root` maxWidth), consider whether to rename/generalize it (e.g. to something like `GROUP_RESERVED_WIDTH` or similar) versus leaving two separately-named constants with the same value — use your own judgement on which reads more clearly, but don't introduce a second, independently-typed copy of the same `calc(4 * var(--zimm-scale-1200))` expression if a shared name is cleaner. Either way, add a comment at the `root` part explaining why this cap exists: without it, the label row's truncation CSS has no width to truncate against, since `root` otherwise sizes to its widest child with no ceiling.

**Explicitly confirm this doesn't change the non-paginated swatches row's own sizing behaviour** — that part was deliberately left to size naturally to actual content in an earlier round, and that must remain true. This fix operates one level up, on `root`'s own outer bound, not on how the swatches row itself sizes within that bound.

## Required verification — real browser, not jsdom reasoning, matching how this exact bug was originally found

Reproduce the failure first (temporarily, to confirm you're testing the right thing), then confirm the fix:

1. Using the same technique the prior Tester used (render the component with a long `selectedName`, e.g. 60-70+ characters, no external width constraint — matching how the `Paginated` or `Default` story would render it in actual Storybook), confirm that BEFORE your fix the name renders at full width (no truncation, component grows past 192px). You can do this via a quick throwaway check — Playwright/Chromium is available and has been used successfully by prior rounds this session for exactly this kind of real-rendering verification.
2. Apply your fix, re-render the identical scenario, confirm the name now truncates with an ellipsis and the component's overall rendered width does not exceed the 192px cap.
3. Add or extend a real Vitest test in `index.test.tsx` asserting this: render with a long `selectedName` and assert via `getComputedStyle` that the root/label element's `maxWidth` resolves to the expected `calc(...)` string (matching the existing style of assertion already used in this file's width-stability test from the prior round — read that test for the pattern). A jsdom-only assertion on the declared `maxWidth` value is meaningful here (unlike the `_focusVisible` case in a separate fix elsewhere, jsdom's `getComputedStyle` DOES correctly echo back a component's own declared CSS custom-property-based values for properties like `width`/`maxWidth`, as already proven by the prior round's own width-stability test) — you do not need a real browser for the automated regression test itself, only for your own manual confirmation that the fix visually works, which real-browser tools are for.
4. Confirm the existing width-stability test (from the immediately prior round, asserting the paginated case's width stays constant across pages) still passes unmodified — this fix must not interact badly with that one.

## What NOT to do

Do not touch `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmColourSwatch/` (Step 2, separately being fixed in a parallel track for an unrelated focus-outline bug — do not touch this file, a conflict here would be a real problem). Do not touch `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx`. Do not touch `overrides/app/theme/foundation/`. Do not re-litigate the pagination-selection fix or the focus-story split from prior rounds — both independently verified correct, leave them alone.

## Verification — run yourself, report exact output

```
npx tsc --noEmit
npm run lint
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.test.tsx
npm run test
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
```

Baselines right now: tsc 0 errors; scoped test file currently 11/11 (you're adding at least 1 new test); full suite 28 files/429 tests before this round; lint 20/4/16 exit 1 unchanged; audit:tokens 4/22 exit 1 unchanged, none in this component.

Report back: the exact constant name/value used, confirmation only `zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts` and `index.test.tsx` were changed, your real-browser before/after evidence (actual observations, not assumptions), and the new/extended test's exact assertion.

4	 * Recipe for the PDP colour-swatch group — the "Colour: Bay Blue" label row, and (when there is

10	 * 40000307:13867 ("ColourOptions"), within Zimmermann_Design_System_2026.
11	 *
12	 * Six parts:
13	 *   - `root` — outer vertical flex container: the label row above, the swatches row below.
14	 *   - `label` — the label row ("labelContainer" in Figma): the label-group (the two
15	 *     "Colour:"/name text pieces — laid out via a plain Chakra-prop wrapper in the component
16	 *     itself, not a seventh part here; see index.tsx's own comment for why) plus the pagination
17	 *     controls, right-aligned purely via the label-group's own `flex: 1 0 0` rather than an
18	 *     absolute-position hack.
19	 *   - `labelName` — the dynamic colour-name text specifically (e.g. "Bay Blue"). Gets its own
20	 *     part, unlike the static "Colour:" piece beside it, because it alone carries the
21	 *     Figma-mandated truncation behaviour: "If Label/Colour name is longer, use truncation"
22	 *     (this node's own interaction annotation).
23	 *   - `swatches` — the horizontal row of rendered ZimmColourSwatch children. Once paginated
24	 *     (`isPaginated`), reserves a fixed page-width footprint regardless of how many items the
25	 *     current window actually renders — see its own baseStyle comment below for the layout bug
26	 *     this prevents.
27	 *   - `pagination` — wrapper around the two chevron buttons.
28	 *   - `pageButton` — each individual chevron button (24x24, holding a 16px ZimmIcon).
29	 */
30	
31	/**
32	 * Matches `SWATCHES_PER_PAGE` in this component's own index.tsx (Figma's own interaction
33	 * annotation: "Pagination appears if there are more than 4 swatches"). Kept as its own literal
34	 * here rather than imported across files — this recipe stays a self-contained, co-located file,
35	 * the same precedent the sibling zimmColourSwatch.css.ts already sets for a state-dependent
36	 * baseStyle function. If `SWATCHES_PER_PAGE` in index.tsx ever changes, update this to match.
37	 */
38	const PAGE_SIZE = 4;
39	
40	/**
41	 * A full page's reserved width: PAGE_SIZE swatches at the atom's own fixed 48px width
42	 * (`--zimm-scale-1200` — see zimmColourSwatch.css.ts's `swatch.width`), with no per-swatch gap
43	 * (`swatches.gap` below is 0, same as the atom's own adjacency). Applied only once paginated —
44	 * see the `swatches` part below.
45	 */
46	const PAGINATED_SWATCHES_WIDTH = `calc(${PAGE_SIZE} * var(--zimm-scale-1200))`;
47	
48	export const ZimmColourSwatchGroup = {
49	  parts: ['root', 'label', 'labelName', 'swatches', 'pagination', 'pageButton'],
50	
51	  baseStyle: ({ isPaginated }: { isPaginated?: boolean }): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
52	    root: {
53	      display: 'flex',
54	      flexDirection: 'column',
55	      // 8px between the label row and the swatches row. No background here — background lives
56	      // per-swatch, already handled by the atom's own recipe.
57	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
58	    },
59	
60	    label: {
61	      display: 'flex',
62	      alignItems: 'center',
63	      // 24px. Matches spacing.xl exactly, so the named step is used rather than the numerically
64	      // identical --zimm-scale-600 alias — see bottomBar.css.ts's own `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`
65	      // usage for the same 24px value elsewhere in this codebase.
66	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)',
67	      // 8px between the label-group and the pagination controls.
68	      gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xs)',
69	    },
70	
71	    labelName: {
72	      textStyle: 'caption',
73	      color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
74	      // The truncating half of the label-group's two text pieces (the static "Colour:" text
75	      // beside it never truncates — see index.tsx). `flex: 1 0 0` lets it consume the
76	      // label-group's remaining width; `minWidth: 0` is required for a flex item to actually
77	      // shrink below its content size instead of overflowing; the rest is the standard
78	      // single-line-ellipsis triad.
79	      flex: '1 0 0',
80	      minWidth: 0,
81	      overflow: 'hidden',
82	      textOverflow: 'ellipsis',
83	      whiteSpace: 'nowrap',
84	    },
85	
86	    swatches: {
87	      display: 'flex',
88	      // Non-paginated (<= SWATCHES_PER_PAGE populated colours): sizes naturally to however many
89	      // swatches are actually present. Unchanged, deliberately out of scope for this fix — there
90	      // is no confirmed design value either way for a 2- or 3-colour row's width, so nothing was
91	      // invented here.
92	      //
93	      // Paginated (> SWATCHES_PER_PAGE populated colours, windowed to a fixed PAGE_SIZE-wide
94	      // slice per page): a plain `100%` here resolves against `root`'s own width — but `root` has
95	      // no explicit width of its own, so it auto-fits to its widest child, which is this very
96	      // element. That circular relationship meant the *rendered* width tracked how many items the
97	      // current window actually held (192px for a full 4-item page, 96px for a 2-item final
98	      // page), so `root` — and `label` above it, itself 100% of that same `root` — visibly
99	      // resized between pages. Confirmed directly in a running Storybook: the pagination chevrons
100	      // jumped position between the two pages of the `Paginated` story. Reserving
101	      // PAGINATED_SWATCHES_WIDTH regardless of the current page's real item count breaks that
102	      // loop — the footprint stays constant across every page, full or partial. A partial final
103	      // page's unused space simply remains empty to the right: the flex default
104	      // `justify-content: flex-start` already left-aligns the rendered items, so nothing further
105	      // is needed for that.
106	      width: isPaginated ? PAGINATED_SWATCHES_WIDTH : '100%',
107	      ...(isPaginated ? { minWidth: PAGINATED_SWATCHES_WIDTH } : {}),
108	      // Confirmed directly off the Figma export, not a stylistic default: the 4-swatch example
109	      // measures exactly 192px total width for four 48px-wide swatches (4 x 48, no gap
110	      // contribution) — swatches sit directly adjacent. Do not add a gap here; that would be a
111	      // real deviation from the design, not a stylistic default.
112	      gap: 0,
113	    },
114	
115	    pagination: {
116	      display: 'flex',
117	      alignItems: 'center',
118	      // No inter-button gap value exists in the Figma export handed to this step — left at the
119	      // flex default (no `gap` declared at all) rather than invented. Revisit if a designer
120	      // confirms a real value.
121	    },
122	
123	    pageButton: {
124	      display: 'flex',
125	      alignItems: 'center',
126	      justifyContent: 'center',
127	      width: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px
128	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // 24px
129	      // Resets the native <button> UA chrome so the box is exactly the 24x24 the design calls
130	      // for, with the 16px ZimmIcon centred inside it by the flex alignment above.
131	      padding: 0,
132	      border: 'none',
133	      background: 'none',
134	      cursor: 'pointer',
135	      // No confirmed Figma spec for a disabled visual treatment on this control — same "leave an
136	      // unspecified visual state alone rather than invent one" precedent as swatch-group's own
137	      // disabled colour logic (see this codebase's Known Gaps notes). The native `disabled`
138	      // attribute (set in index.tsx) already makes the control genuinely inert and announces as
139	      // disabled to assistive tech; only the cursor affordance is set here, which is a UX
140	      // keyword, not a design token.
141	      _disabled: {
142	        cursor: 'not-allowed',
143	      },
144	      // Same uniform ring every other interactive control in ui-kits/ uses (zimmColourSwatch,
145	      // zimmNavItem) — --zimm-focus-ring already composites the border-width/colour pair.
146	      _focusVisible: {
147	        outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
148	        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
149	      },
150	    },
151	  }),
152	};
